meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (nationally uniform registry; Cámaras de Comercio territorial competence)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition; unitary national system; commercial law codified in the Código de Comercio, Decree 410 of 1971)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 15 May 2012)
Colombia–European Union–Peru–Ecuador Multiparty Trade Agreement (applied since 2013)
Colombia–Canada Free Trade Agreement (in force 15 August 2011)
Colombia–Korea Free Trade Agreement (in force 15 July 2016)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 1258 of 2008 (S.A.S. regime); Código de Comercio Decree 410 of 1971 arts. 98-118 (corporate denomination); Decree 1074 of 2015 (national registry regulation); Law 2010 of 2019 (AML/CFT duties for the real sector); Decree 1674 of 2021 and DIAN Resolution 164 of 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUBF); Decree 830 of 2021 (Sarlaft adoption for Colombian legal entities); Law 526 of 1999 and Law 1121 of 2006 (UIAF and money-laundering criminal framework); Circular Externa 029 of 2014 (SFC, applicable by analogy to financial counterparties).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Legal Representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal) of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) granted by foreign shareholders to the Colombian incorporator or corporate attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Constitutional instrument (estatutos S.A.S.) executed as Documento Privado with authenticated signatures (rúbrica)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Colombian notary público and corporate founders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial authentication; no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation (traducción oficial) of all foreign-language corporate, POA, and UBO identification documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Colombian authorized translator (traductor oficial) with notarial certification of signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification; no apostille required on translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies of foreign shareholders, administrators, and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority; notarized copy certification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, legal representatives, administrators, and UBOs of the S.A.S. against (i) Colombian official state lists — Procuraduría General de la Nación, Contraloría General de la República, Fiscalía General de la Nación, and UIAF PEP database; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (iii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists; (iv) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists; (v) Interpol red notices; and (vi) domestic Colombian 'Listas Nacionales' (PEP and sanctioned persons). Screening must be repeated upon any equity amendment, administrator change, UBO variation, or high-risk transactional trigger per Decree 830 of 2021 and the entity's internal Sarlaft protocol. For B2B marketplace merchants and cross-border payment rails (Alibaba Pay, SWIFT wire), enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, virtual-asset-related counterparties, and inconsistent beneficial-ownership chains.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) via the competent Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / www.rues.org.co) — online homonimia consultation and issuance of the Certificado de Homonimia.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be registered using the Latin (Spanish) alphabet; Spanish is the operative registry language and names are indexed under Spanish orthography. The distinctive element ('denominación') may include foreign words only if expressed in standard Latin characters and free of misleading, vulgar, or publicly suggestive meanings. The registered name must conclude with the token 'S.A.S.' or the full phrase 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: State or public-authority terms: 'Nacional', 'Presidencia', 'Ministerio', 'Gobernación', 'Nación', 'Departamento', 'Municipio', 'Policía', 'Fuerza Pública' — require prior authorization from the relevant state entity.

Regulated financial and health-sector terms: 'Banco', 'Seguro', 'Previsión', 'Fondo de Pensiones', 'Cooperativa', 'Mutual', 'Entidad de Salud' — require prior approval from the Superintendencia Financiera or Superintendencia Nacional de Salud, as applicable.
International-organization and protected-symbol references: 'Naciones Unidas', 'OEA', 'Cruz Roja', 'Unicef', national symbols and official heraldry — prohibited absent institutional consent.

Identical or confusingly similar denominations to an existing registered company name, protected trademark, or well-known commercial establishment within the same RUES index — rejection without consent or coexistence agreement.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) file a 'recurso de reposición' before the same Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days of notification, with full legal grounds and curative documentation; (ii) file a subsidiary 'recurso de apelación' before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) for definitive administrative resolution; or (iii) initiate a fresh homonimia application under an alternative distinct denomination. If rejection is based on an identical registered trademark, obtain a written coexistence authorization from the trademark owner or commence trademark cancellation/nullity proceedings before SIC. The homonimia certificate is non-extendable; re-application is required after the 30-day validity window at the standard registry tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The S.A.S. must designate a real 'domicilio' inside Colombian territory; a virtual office or coworking address may be registered provided it offers physical mail reception, a verifiable address for judicial notice (notificaciones judiciales), and a DIAN-recognized fiscal address. For a low-risk, unlicensed B2B cross-border platform, virtual office acceptance is administratively viable, but merchant payment acquirers and bank onboarding (Alibaba Pay, SWIFT wire) may require evidence of operating substance or an additional physical nearshore development/digital operations center address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5–10% annualized) for an unlicensed, low-risk-standard e-commerce S.A.S.; however, DIAN may conduct fiscal address verification (verificación de domicilio) and the Cámara de Comercio may perform sporadic registry inspections. Unannounced on-site inspection probability materially increases upon tax red flags, UBO inconsistencies, or AML reporting triggers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance — Certificado de Homonimia and RUES online pre-check
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio competente (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the S.A.S. incorporation private document (documento privado de constitución) in the Registro Mercantil
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry tariff scaled to registered capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization (rúbrica) of signatures on the constitutional document and POA
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Colombian notary public of the Circuito

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting and review of S.A.S. by-laws, UBO clauses, governance, and pre-incorporation due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee / hourly rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation (traducción oficial) of foreign corporate documents and powers of attorney
Apostille or consular legalization of foreign corporate documents (certificate of good standing, POA, passport copies)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin jurisdiction / Colombian consulate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUBF / UBO registration (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales)
RUT and provisional NIT pre-registration (pre-rut / asignación de NIT)
Digital signature / electronic certificate for online filings with DIAN and RUES
Registered virtual office / domicilio service including mail reception and service-of-process address
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Coworking / virtual office provider with legal mail services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for ancillary notarial, courier, and tariff adjustments

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), arts. 1-48; Código de Comercio, Decreto 410 de 1971, arts. 110-116 (commercial registry); Decreto 1074 de 2015 (Regulatory Decree of Commerce); combined with the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — Registro Mercantil (electronic single-window RUES portal of the Chamber of Commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) filed with the Chamber of Commerce; public deed (Escritura Pública) is required only when real property or regulated in-kind assets are contributed as capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital: the S.A.S. capital is freely stipulated in the bylaws; paid contributions are due on the agreed date and in all cases within two (2) years of incorporation (Ley 1258/2008, art. 5). No escrow account or blocked capital deposit is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. By unanimous written consent of the shareholders, the following resolutions are adopted. RESOLVED: (1) The subscription and payment of shares set out in the articles of incorporation are approved and recorded in the Share Register. (2) The registered office of the Company is fixed at [Address], Bogotá D.C., Colombia, governing all corporate and tax communications. (3) [Name of Manager] is appointed Legal Representative, with broad powers for corporate acts, contracts, and banking procedures. (4) The Legal Representative is authorized to complete all registration formalities before the Chamber of Commerce and the DIAN on behalf of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — virtual certificate service (www.ccb.org.co / RUES portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Chamber of Commerce online services, select the certificate of homonymy module, enter up to three proposed corporate names and the incorporation type (S.A.S.), pay the nominal search fee via PSE, and download the formal Certificado de Homonimia confirming the selected name is not pre-occupied.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name variants (up to three)
Power of attorney when filing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first-choice name is already registered, the portal automatically checks the alternates; reserve an unused substitute name and obtain a fresh homonymy certificate before continuing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the incorporation instrument (Documento Privado de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders (or notary public only if real estate/in-kind regulated assets are contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the S.A.S. bylaws containing the corporate name, corporate purpose (ISIC 4791 electronic B2B marketplace platform operation), subscribed capital, share classes, representation rules, and the two-year capital payment schedule. Execute the private document by the signature of all shareholders, attesting their legal capacity. If in-kind assets are contributed, notarize and authenticate the document before signature.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of each shareholder (cédula or passport)
Bank or appraisal evidence for any in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Errors in the instrument are corrected by executing an addendum (aclaración) before the same notary or, if already filed, by submitting a rectification document with the Chamber of Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registry filing and issuance of the certification (Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — Registro Mercantil / RUES electronic filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit through the Chamber of Commerce virtual filing desk: the executed private incorporation document, the homonymy certificate, shareholder identification, and the RUES pre-form. Pay the registration fee plus the impuesto de registro (registration tax of 0.4%-0.7% on the subscribed capital, as per the current municipal tariff) via PSE or authorized financial institutions. Upon approval, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal and assigns the initial provisional NIT.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fee and registration tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues observations, file a solicitud de corrección or recurso de reposición within ten (10) business days with the corrected instruments; the Chamber's advisory service assists in curing all observations before the legal deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration — NIT assignment and RUT enrollment with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — online RUT module at www.dian.gov.co
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the provisional NIT and the Chamber registration certificate, access the DIAN electronic portal, complete the RUT form, select applicable tax responsibilities (corporate income tax, VAT, withholding agent, and electronic invoicing obligation), validate the legal representative's identity, and download the definitive RUT certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Company e-mail address and registered-office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NIT/RUT validation fails due to a discrepancy in names, file a Corrección de RUT with the revised Chamber certificate; if biometric validation fails, schedule an in-person DIAN appointment for manual enrollment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of corporate bank account and payment of subscribed capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercially licensed bank (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda, Banco de Bogotá); no government agency involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the incorporation evidence to the bank, complete KYC/AML onboarding for the entity and its beneficial owners, and open a corporate current account. Disburse the subscribed capital into the account, obtain a deposit receipt or bank certificate, and update the payment records in the corporate Share Register.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Board resolution appointing the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, supply sworn source-of-funds statements, shareholder bank references, and a corporate structure chart; alternatively, open the account at another licensed commercial bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration obligations — electronic invoicing, accounting books and municipal registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (electronic invoicing); Cámara de Comercio (rubric of accounting books); municipal tax authority (Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda for Bogotá — ICA registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enable DIAN electronic invoicing by accepting the technical parameters and obtaining an invoice certificate from an authorized technology provider. Purchase the accounting books (Libro de Actas, Libro de Accionistas, Libro Diario, Libro Mayor) and submit them to the Chamber for official stamping. Enroll in the municipal Industry and Commerce Tax (ICA) registry and complete the corresponding declaration obligation.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Electronic invoicing software contract or certificate
ICA enrollment form and registered-office lease proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For DIAN rejection of the invoicing authorization, correct the technical certificate and resubmit the electronic-invoicing habilitation; for municipal registration errors, file a corrective ICA declaration with the Secretaría de Hacienda and pay any applicable surcharge within the first month to avoid penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) — consumer protection and e-commerce regulatory oversight; Ministry of Information and Communications Technologies (MinTIC) for digital platform notification, if triggered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial operating license is required for a digital B2B marketplace. Compliance is governed instead by SIC e-commerce regulations (Ley 527 de 1999, Ley 1480 de 2011) on information, contractual terms, revocation mechanisms, and by MinTIC's optional digital-economy platform notification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) / Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente, Bogotá D.C.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is a virtual, non-industrial marketplace with no construction, manufacturing, or pollutant discharge; no EIA study, environmental license, or prior environmental certificate is required under Decreto 1076 de 2015.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None applicable to the server-based commercial activity. Administrative office waste must comply with municipal solid-waste rules (Ley 1259 de 2008) and color-coded sorting standards (Resolución 2184 de 2019); no process wastewater, volatile organic compounds, or regulated air emissions are generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises require an active annual fire-safety certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) issued by the competent fire brigade; the employer must implement the SG-SST occupational health and safety system (Decreto 1072 de 2015) including occupational-medical assessments and an emergency response plan; if the office accommodates public traffic, obtain the sanitary concept (concepto sanitario) from the local health authority. Structural-load and land-use compliance is confirmed through the landlord's building occupancy certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); primary online portal: www.dian.gov.co; transactional portal: www.muisca.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor incorporates a Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) before the Cámara de Comercio, then completes the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) application with DIAN to obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria), which serves as the unified tax ID for income tax, IVA, withholding taxes, and electronic invoicing. A foreign enterprise with no Colombian branch may alternatively obtain an NIT under the DIAN simplified registration regime for non-resident digital service providers, which requires the appointment of a local legal representative and the issuance of a virtual RUT. No minimum paid-in capital is required for the S.A.S.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the Colombian S.A.S. is a resident legal entity taxed on worldwide net income at the corporate rate; pass-through treatment is unavailable; dividends distributed to non-residents are subject to final withholding at the applicable treaty or statutory rate)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or look-through election exists under Colombian law. Statutory elections that remain available are: (i) the consolidated income tax return option for subsidiaries meeting the 51% ownership continuity test under Articles 128-133 of the Estatuto Tributario; (ii) the SIMPLE presumptive regime election for qualifying micro/small businesses with ordinary gross income below 80,000 UVT (approx. COP 3.77 billion for 2024, annually adjusted); and (iii) the Colombian holding company regime (Régimen CHC) election for pure holding S.A.S. vehicles. Hybrid mismatch outcomes under Law 2010 of 2019 and Law 2277 of 2022 are policed by disallowance rules rather than activated by taxpayer elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto al Valor Agregado) - Value Added Tax; the national consumption tax (Impuesto Nacional al Consumo) applies to certain enumerated services but is secondary to IVA for B2B platform activities
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold in local currency: every Colombian legal entity, including an S.A.S. marketplace operator, must register in the RUT and as an IVA responsible taxpayer from its first corporate act. Non-resident digital service providers are likewise subject to mandatory DIAN registration without any de minimis turnover exemption and invoice from the first Colombian-destination digital service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Factura Electrónica de Venta is compulsory and operates as a near-real-time fiscal clearance system. Invoices must be generated in an XML/JSON file, signed with a DIAN-approved digital signature certificate, and transmitted through DIAN web services (REST/SOAP API) or a certified technology provider; DIAN validates the invoice and returns the CUNE (Código Único de Numeración); a QR code and the CUNE must be printed on the invoice. Export invoices and documents supporting purchases from non-residents use the CUDS/CUFE codes and must be transmitted to DIAN with the relevant annexes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Colombian S.A.S. that operates an electronic B2B wholesale marketplace may issue its platform commissions, listing, and subscription invoices at the 0% IVA export rate under Article 481 of the Estatuto Tributario when the recipient is not domiciled in Colombia and the digital intermediation service is economically used abroad. The claim also requires a written export service contract, a zero-rated invoice, and the channeling and repatriation of proceeds through the Colombian foreign exchange market within the applicable deadline (180 days for goods; services must satisfy the applicable Banco de la República term). The zero rate is denied if the counterparty is a Colombian resident user, if the platform facilitates consumption within Colombia, or if physical goods are sold without an actual customs export declaration and departure from the national territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DEX/DAB) issued by DIAN customs authorities for physical goods exported through the marketplace
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / ground waybill) demonstrating the foreign destination and physical exit of goods

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas / Declaración de Cambio) proving the currency was repatriated and the export proceeds were dedicated to the Colombian foreign exchange market
Export service contract naming the non-domiciled buyer and evidencing the extraterritorial use of the platform service
Zero-rated commercial export invoice carrying the CUNE and the 0% IVA annotation
Commercial invoice, packing list, and the relevant INCOTERM supporting the sale for customs provenance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN subjects exporter VAT refund applications to documentary pre-verification and selective post-audit. If the export condition is not sustained, DIAN retroactively assesses the 19% IVA on the gross proceeds together with moratory interest under Article 635 E.T., imposes the inaccuracy sanction of 50% to 160% of the understated tax under Article 648 E.T., and may apply the additional penalty for false operations; in customs export scenarios, sanctions include seizure of goods and customs infraction penalties, potentially escalating to criminal proceedings under the customs regime. Failure to comply with the 180-day forex repatriation requirement rebuts the export evidence and opens the clawback within the five-year statute of limitations, and fraudulent zero-rating documentation attracts criminal exposure before the DIAN and public prosecutors.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (the Central Bank of Colombia), acting through the Régimen Cambiario built on Ley 9 de 1991, Decreto 1735 de 1993 and Resolución Externa No. 1 de 2018; enforcement of FX channeling obligations is delegated to the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), while the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia supervises the authorized MCR intermediaries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso is freely convertible for current-account transactions, including service exports and after-tax remittances of profits, provided settlement is executed through the Mercado Cambiario (MCR). Capital-account operations (initial FDI subscription, equity increases, external loans) remain fully deregulated today but require formal filing of the 'Declaración de Cambio – Formulario No. 4' with the Banco de la República through a licensed intermediary; a foreign investor that completes the Formulario No. 4 registration on or before the settlement date may later remit up to 100% of after-tax distributable profits without prior approval, but failure to register the investment before repatriation exposes the entity to FX-infringement fines and potential rejection of the outward remittance by the local intermediary. No general exchange-control freeze currently applies to ordinary current or capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters of platform services must channel 100% of the aggregate foreign-exchange proceeds through the MCR within a maximum statutory period of six (6) months from the date of invoice or service completion; proceeds received by the S.A.S. through offshore collection wallets (Alibaba Pay) become subject to the same deadline once settlement takes place, and the funds must be credited to an MCR-authorized local bank account before any 'Declaración de Cambio' can be filed. There is no minimum mandatory conversion ratio to COP: upon channeling, the exporter holds free disposal over the currency and may either (i) sell it to the local intermediary against COP or (ii) retain it in an authorized foreign-currency deposit account; direct retention abroad beyond the deadline is a violation subject to DIAN fines of up to 200% of the un-channeled amount.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD/COP Current Account (Cuenta Corriente) with a segregated FDI capital-channeling sub-ledger
Operational USD/COP Current Account (Cuenta Corriente) with a segregated FDI capital-channeling sub-ledger

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM as a standalone treasury rail and MEDIUM-HIGH as a settlement gateway. Offshore EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Alibaba Pay) are neither Colombian-licensed MCR institutions nor authorized FX intermediaries; using them as the final deposit location technically violates the channeling duty under the foreign-currency channeling provisions of Resolución Externa No. 1 de 2018 and can trigger DIAN non-compliance fines of up to 200% of the underlying amount. Compliant use is therefore restricted to: (a) collecting B2B marketplace receipts from foreign buyers, (b) routing weekly sweeps to the Colombian USD account of the S.A.S., and (c) maintaining settlement reports that reconcile Alibaba Pay payout files with the Declaración de Cambio forms filed by the local bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement that every foreign director appear in person; however, Colombian anti-money-laundering standards (Circular Básica Jurídica and Law 2155 de 2021 biometric identification rules for financial services) and the practical onboarding policies of tier-1 banks require at least one locally identifiable legal representative to attend a face-to-face KYC interview before the USD account is opened. Remote opening via apostilled general power of attorney and video-conference KYC is accepted by Bancolombia and Davivienda for qualified foreign officers, yet a physical visit of the non-resident shareholder or a walk-in to the bank's international desk remains the fastest de-risking pathway during the first six months of the relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: the S.A.S. is held by non-resident shareholders whose ultimate natural-owner identification, source of wealth and residence tax IDs are incomplete in the share registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated corporate chart with full UBO identification (beneficial ownership above 5%), bank-grade source-of-wealth statement, notarized certificate evidencing the chain of title, current passport copies, and sworn beneficial-ownership questionnaire under Law 2010 de 2019.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket marketplace remittances from foreign buyers received via Alibaba Pay create commingling and potential undeclared-sales red flags in the bank's transaction monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: B2B platform seller and buyer agreements, seller KYC register, platform dashboard statements reconciled with SWIFT feeds, per-invoice electronic-invoice (factura electrónica) sample extracts, and the ongoing Declaración de Cambio queue evidencing timely channeling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital wire arrives from a nominal remitter different from the registered shareholder or from an EMI pool (shared settlement account), triggering enhanced due diligence and a possible opening hard-stop.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 field-50 trace evidencing the registered shareholder as remitter, shareholder resolution on capital subscription, bank reference letter from the originator, pre-funding bank statements, and proof of Formulario No. 4 investor registration filed with the Banco de la República on the settlement date.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of local substance (single foreign director, no payroll, no physical office) leading to classification as a shell or surrogate account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial-registry certificate (Cámara de Comercio), valid RUT, lease or co-working agreement, social-security contributions for the local officer, management accounts, and a substance memorandum describing the marketplace's operational middleware, seller onboarding and cash-flow management.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for FDI wiring: the non-resident shareholder originates an SWIFT MT103 from its individual or corporate bank account to the S.A.S. USD account at a tier-1 Colombian bank, with Field 70 citing 'DECLARACION DE CAMBIO FORM 4 – INVERSION INTERNACIONAL – [SHAREHOLDER NAME] – [RUT]'; the receiving bank presents Formulario No. 4 in the Banco de la República system no later than the following business day of value date; funds received from third-party wallets or EMIs without documentary name-match to the registered shareholder are rejected or held under enhanced due-diligence until the source-of-funds bundle is accepted; for operating receipts from the marketplace, the entity maintains a monthly canalización register linking Alibaba Pay settlement files to each local bank SWIFT or CST statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing is split into three rails: (1) domestic seller payouts in COP executed via TEF/ACH Colombia from the operational account; (2) cross-border vendor and software-services payments routed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the USD account; and (3) goods-backed trades raised under a Commercial Letter of Credit (confirmed or advised by the local bank) when the underlying purchase agreement requires standard trade instruments; all outbound disbursements require the matching electronic invoice or factura and the applicable customs declaration, and USD wire transfers above USD 10,000 are subject to the bank's enhanced transaction monitoring and UIAF notification thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/COP forward contracts executed with MCR-authorized intermediaries (Bancolombia, Banco de Bogotá, BBVA Colombia) hedging identified expected proceeds and payable invoices

Non-deliverable USD/COP forwards (NDFs) transacted offshore as overlay hedges for volatile cash flows, subject to documentation of the underlying commercial exposure and local counterparty reporting requirements
USD/COP foreign-exchange swaps and cross-currency swaps with licensed local banks to bridge the timing mismatch between USD collections (Alibaba Pay sweeps) and COP operational costs
USD/COP futures and options traded through the Bolsa de Valores de Colombia (BVC) cleared derivative market, limited to the volume of the company's underlying open trade positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the Mercantile Registry (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction at the registered office address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal imposes a penalty of 15% of the applicable tariff plus interest; persistent non-renewal for five years leads to administrative strike-off and loss of commercial capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements and approval minutes (Depósito de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction at the registered office address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval by 31 March; deposit with the Chamber of Commerce within one month after approval, normally by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit prevents lawful registry renewal, exposes the SAS to fines by the Superintendencia de Sociedades of up to 200 SMMLV, and may trigger administrative dissolution after repeated omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Shareholders' Meeting and corporate minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held by 31 March each year; minutes must approve financial statements and record management actions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of a valid meeting invalidates the financial statement deposit; continued failure permits court-ordered meeting authorization and regulatory intervention by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax information return (Información Exógena) covering shareholders, payments and third-party transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 14 June and 16 August, based on the last digit of the NIT; final deadline 31 August
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts 1% monthly fines up to 12% of amounts reported, or a minimum of 20 UVT; inaccurate filings incur 5,000 UVT penalties under Article 651 E.T.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) report to DIAN (Reporte de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN Superintendencia de Sociedades and corporate UBO records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 July, or within two months after any change in ultimate beneficial ownership under DIAN Resolution 164/2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting or inaccurate UBO data triggers fines up to 15,000 UVT (approximately USD 178,000) and potential criminal exposure for deliberate concealment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Share transfer registration and shareholders' register confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio for share endorsements; DIAN for corresponding UBO update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each transfer must be recorded in the shareholder ledger promptly and reflected in DIAN's UBO update cycle; annual confirmation completed at the 31 March shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered transfers are ineffective against third parties; failure to update the UBO declaration exposes the SAS to the 15,000 UVT penalty for each unreported beneficial owner.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A licensed Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) must be appointed if, in the prior fiscal year, gross assets or gross revenues exceed 5,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.6 million), if the SAS has more than 50 shareholders, or if the company is a parent or subordinate entity subject to consolidated group thresholds under Law 43/1990.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS as adopted by Colombia under Decree 2420/2015 for public-interest and large entities; otherwise, small and mid-sized SAS entities apply IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para PYMES) using CTCP-issued official standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must maintain a current shareholder ledger establishing each owner's nominal and ultimate beneficial interest, identifying individuals with at least 10% participation or control. Annually, no later than the applicable DIAN schedule, the company must confirm or update its UBO declaration through DIAN's mandatory electronic form; share transfers executed after the annual filing trigger a supplementary declaration within two months.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,200 per year for a Colombian registered office and compliance agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 7,500 per year for a certified statutory audit when thresholds are met

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (general corporate income tax rate effective from tax year 2023 onward under Law 2277 of 2022; no CREE surcharge applies to a standard S.A.S. operating an electronic B2B wholesale platform)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory exemptions and deductions that may reduce effective CIT: (i) 'Orange Economy' consecutive 7-year income tax exemption for qualifying innovative/creative technology ventures, subject to prior SAS incorporation, innovation certification and DIAN compliance conditions; (ii) 150% additional payroll deduction for base wages paid to employees under 28 years of age or employees with disabilities; (iii) 100% extra deduction for verified investments in research, technological development and innovation; (iv) accelerated depreciation and 30% to 100% investment deductions for qualifying fixed asset acquisitions (e.g., B2B logistics and platform infrastructure) as permitted for the tax year; all exemptions require prior factual demonstration and cannot be presumed by a non-resident owner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) for legal entities, submitted exclusively through the DIAN electronic filing portal 'MUISCA' (Módulo para la Gestión de Ingresos, Servicios y Conocimiento); mandatory digital certification and e-signature via the legal representative's registered electronic signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year ending 31 December for the standard S.A.S.); the DIAN publishes an annual staggered filing calendar and the same calendar applies for each S.A.S. based on its NIT final digits.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due no later than the date assigned by DIAN based on the last two digits of the NIT, as published in the annual filing schedule, generally falling between early March and early May of the year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., tax year 2024 returns are due on the assigned calendar days in 2025). A non-resident owner must ensure the Colombian legal representative monitors the published schedule; no blanket extension is available except by DIAN resolution for force majeure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT of the taxpayer: the 9-digit Colombian tax identification number plus verification digit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the S.A.S. Colombian NIT exactly as registered in the RUES registry; a foreign parent company's NIT or branch code must not be substituted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Año gravable (taxable year): the closed fiscal year for which the return is filed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the S.A.S. has not been authorized by DIAN for a non-calendar year-end; standard penetration is January 1 to December 31.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross operating income: all Colombian-source revenue from the B2B marketplace store (platform commissions, seller subscriptions, logistics fees, marketing services, listing fees and transaction-value components).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only revenue recognized by the Colombian S.A.S.; any income attributed to or billed through the foreign parent must be backed by an intercompany agreement priced at arm's length and disclosed in the Local File.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Devoluciones, rebajas y descuentos (returns, rebates and discounts): allowable reductions only when supported by electronic invoices (factura electrónica) or equivalent DIAN-approved credit notes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Discounts granted to foreign B2B buyers require formal debit/credit notes cross-referenced to the original invoice and must be consistent with group pricing policies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales: acquisition cost of goods/services sold through the marketplace, including customs duties and import costs, validated against warehouse and logistics records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party purchases from the foreign parent or group sourcing companies must be substantiated with contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and customs declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative and selling expenses: payroll, IT infrastructure, cloud services, professional fees, marketing, rents and other operating costs causally linked to Colombian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office cost recharges, management fees and remote-technology service fees payable to a non-resident parent are deductible only if the service is real, benefits the Colombian entity and the payment is made through a Colombian bank account with exchange-control declaration; substandard documentation leads to add-back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rentas exentas (exempt income): statutory exemptions applied by the taxpayer, including the orange-economy benefit where certified.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident owner may not instruct allocation of foreign-source exempt income to the Colombian entity; any exemption must be created by Colombian law and supported by DIAN rulings or certification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto sobre la renta: tax computed at the 35% statutory rate on the renta líquida gravable after exemptions and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are not claimable on the Colombian return unless a bilateral tax treaty or a DIAN administrative ruling explicitly so permits; otherwise double taxation is resolved only via the dividend withholding mechanics.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retenciones en la fuente aplicadas (withholdings applied): Colombian source withholdings borne by the entity and creditable against final income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only withholdings evidenced by the withholding agent's certificate (certificado de retención) and reflected in the annual exógena information may be credited; a foreign parent cannot transfer its own withheld amounts to the S.A.S. unless contractually borne and documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Saldo a pagar o saldo a favor (balance payable or balance in favor): net income tax obligation after withholdings and advance payments (anticipos).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance in favor requested in cash by the S.A.S. will be accepted only after the relevant exógena information is filed and is subject to DIAN pre-refund review; the non-resident owner must route refunds to a registered Colombian account and may be subject to the 10% dividend withholding on subsequent upstream remittance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the tax payable for each calendar month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% supplementing the tax due, with a minimum penalty of 10 UVT when no tax is due or a loss is reported. Late payment: monthly moratory interest at the DIAN-published rate (approx. 2%–2.5% per month) plus CPI indexation. Material understatement and false information trigger the inexactness penalty of 100% of the difference between the assessed tax and the declared tax, computed on the revised taxable income; criminal tax evasion penalties then apply separately.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends paid to a non-resident shareholder out of profits already subjected to the 35% corporate income tax (Articles 242 and 245 E.T.); 35% withholding applies to distributions made from previously untaxed profits or from earnings classified as exempt where the exemption is not recognized at the source level. Domestic Colombian corporate shareholders receiving dividends from taxed earnings are exempt; the 10% rate is therefore the operative non-resident rate for a standard B2B marketplace S.A.S.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced rate under a DTA in force (Spain, Canada, France, Chile, United Kingdom, Mexico, Switzerland, South Korea): (1) obtain from the home-country competent authority a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) specifically covering the tax year of the dividend distribution; (2) have the TRC apostilled or legalized where required in the beneficiary jurisdiction; (3) provide a beneficial-ownership declaration to the Colombian withholding agent confirming the recipient is the ultimate owner; (4) retain the complete file in Colombia for at least five years and disclose the transaction in the annual exógena information. The reduced treaty rate is applied at source only where the payer receives the TRC before remittance; if the full 10% or 35% is withheld, refund must be pursued by the non-resident through a DIAN refund request (devolución) attaching the TRC, payment voucher and dividend act. No DTA relief is available for Hong Kong, Mainland China, Singapore, or most Latin American recipients without a ratified convention.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on payments abroad: 15% on IP royalties (patents, trademarks, software licensing, know-how and technical assistance fees) and 15% on interest on external debt financing under Articles 406–408 of the Tax Statute. Treaty rates may reduce these amounts (e.g., up to 5%–15% under certain DTAs for financial institutions), but for a Hong Kong or Singapore parent with no DTA, the 15% statutory rate is final and must be withheld at the moment of remittance; the Colombian payer is the statutory withholding agent and is personally liable for the tax if not withheld.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory when the Colombian S.A.S. reports annual gross income equal or superior to COP 2,117,925,000 (equivalent to 45,000 UVT, UVT-2024 = COP 47,065) and executes transactions with related parties or with entities located in jurisdictions treated as tax havens; Master File mandatory when the ultimate parent group's consolidated gross income equals or exceeds COP 470,650,000,000 (equivalent to 10,000,000 UVT-2024). The annual UVT is re-indexed by DIAN each year, so the precise peso threshold must be re-calculated at filing date.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP — Comparable Uncontrolled Price (precio comparable no controlado)
TNMM — Transactional Net Margin Method (margen neto de transacción)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not enforce offshore-format Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); instead, DIAN applies the general anti-abuse doctrine (Article 869 E.T.), the principle of substance over form, and the corporate/veil-piercing rules of Law 1258 of 2008 to invalidate structures without commercial reality. The B2B marketplace S.A.S. must maintain physical or virtual office infrastructure, decision-making personnel, platform IT management, and economic risk absorption in Colombia; the foreign parent must not act as a letterbox. Without demonstrable substance, DIAN can re-characterize the entire platform commercialization structure, deny expense deductions, reframe royalty or service payments as dividends subjected to the 10% or 35% withholding, and impose the 100% inexactness penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of B2B marketplace commissions and fees from the annual return; issuance of false electronic invoices or simulated seller refunds; systematic under-declaration of cross-border SWIFT receipts; diversion of Colombian-source platform revenue to the foreign parent without booking the corresponding income in the S.A.S.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code (Código Penal) Article 402: imprisonment of 48 to 108 months when the tax evaded exceeds 100 legal monthly minimum wages; DIAN inexactness penalty of 100% of the difference between the assessed and declared tax; moratory interest on all underpaid amounts; asset seizure and liquidation proceedings by the DIAN fiscal collection authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and the directors who sign the return are jointly and severally liable; criminal conviction carries imprisonment, travel bans preventing departure from Colombian territory, freezing of personal bank accounts, confiscation of assets, and debarment from commercial activity; Article 43 of Law 1258 of 2008 pierces the S.A.S. veil where the corporate form is used to defraud the treasury.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance (Abuso de Formas Societarias)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the B2B marketplace as a zero-employee, zero-asset nominee entity while the foreign parent executes all contracts, holds bank accounts, and collects payments; receiving dividends or fees from Colombia without any local commercial activity; hiding the Colombian management from tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN rejection of the legal structure under the GAAR and substance-over-form doctrine: inclusion of the full re-characterized gross margin in the S.A.S. taxable income at 35%, disallowance of all rechargeable expenses, 100% inexactness penalty on the resulting tax deficiency, and reclassification of targeted payments as unpermitted dividend remittances with withholding assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the S.A.S. and the foreign parent's shadow directors who act as de facto managers in Colombia face joint and several liability for the entire tax deficiency, civil restitution of diverted assets, judicial intervention orders, and criminal prosecution for fraud where creditors or the tax authority were deceived.
